summary: Norman Fischer is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Colgate University, the University of Iowa, UC Berkeley, and Graduate Theological Union, and under Mel Weitsman and Richard Baker. In 2000, he founded the Everyday Zen Foundation.

Norvin J. Hein was a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied under Franklin Edgerton. He held a post at Yale Divinity School as Associate Professor of Comparative Religion, attested in 1965.

Yoshinari Fuji is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dongguk University in 1986. He held posts at Daegu University, the Institute of Religious Culture, Bukkyo Bunka Kenkyujo, Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College, and Ryukoku University.

Notto R. Thelle is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He was Associate Director at the NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions in 1974 and held a post at the University of Oslo from circa 1986 to 2006.

Noémie Verdon is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne in 2015 under supervisors Johannes Bronkhorst and Charles Genequand, and held a post at Kyoto University attested in 2019.

Noël Péri was a Japanology and Buddhist studies scholar. He taught Western music at Tokyo Fine Arts School (1896–1906), founded Tenchijin and Mélanges japonais, and served as resident (1907) and secretary-librarian (1911) at the École française d'Extrême-Orient.

Nyanaponika Thera was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Nyanatiloka Mahathera, Mahasi Sayadaw, and at the University of Peradeniya. He founded the Buddhist Publication Society, serving as its director and editor (1958–1984) and president (~1958–1988).

Nyingcha Duoji is a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at Boston University and earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2014) under doctoral supervisor Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp and teacher Mark Elliott.
Nyo Shul Lungtok Tenpé Gyaltsen studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and taught Terton Sogyal.

Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Katok and Nyoshul Monasteries and under Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, and Penor Rinpoche.
Nyoten Jimbo was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Baisen Azegami and served as a professor at Komazawa University.

O. M. Moneer was a history, archaeology, and Indology scholar. He served as Curator at the Central Asian Antiquities Museum and was attested in 1939 as Assistant Superintendent, Western Circle, for the Archaeological Survey of India.

Octave Hamelin was a philosophy scholar who studied at Lycée Henri-IV. He held posts at the University of Bordeaux (~1884–1905), the École Normale Supérieure (~1903–1905), and the University of Paris (~1905–1907).

Ogyen Trinley Dorje is an active figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche, Drub Pön Dechen Rinpoche, the 14th Dalai Lama, Dragpa Tenpa Yarpel, Bokar Rinpoche, and Pema Donyo Nyinje.

Olaf Hansen was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1937–1945), the University of Jena, and the Free University of Berlin (~1950–1969).

Olav Hackstein is a linguistics, Iranian, Central Asian, and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Freiburg and UPenn, and held posts at UPenn, Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, the University of Munich, and EPHE.

Ole Holten Pind was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Vienna from circa 2004 to 2009 under doctoral supervisor Ernst Steinkellner, receiving his Dr.phil.

Oleg Grabar was an archaeology and history scholar. He studied at the University of Paris, Harvard, and Princeton, and held posts at the Albright Institute (1953), University of Michigan (1954–1969), Harvard (1969–1990), and IAS (1990–1998).

Oliver Codrington was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Secretary of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1878) and Honorary Librarian of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (attested 1892).

Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Colombo and SOAS. He held posts at the University of Ceylon, University of Pennsylvania, Harvard, and Smith College.
